comparisons.peer_topic: All Other operating loss breakdown for 2024 and 2023
comparisons.peer_summary: All Other operating loss was $4.2 billion in 2024 and $4.4 billion in 2023, primarily consisting of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and stock-based compensation expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD define an 'All Other' segment category to capture results from businesses that are not separately reportable. Intel explicitly lists Altera and Mobileye as components of this 'All Other' category, whereas AMD's 'All Other' operating loss is driven by amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and stock-based compensation, without naming specific subsidiaries like Intel's Altera/Mobileye in this summary. Both disclosures treat these non-reportable elements as a consolidated catch-all for specific corporate-level or non-core operational results.

sentences.text: Our "all other" category includes the results of operations from other non-reportable segments not otherwise presented, including our Altera and Mobileye businesses, start-up businesses that support our initiatives, and historical results of operations from divested businesses.
All Other operating loss of $4.2 billion in 2024 primarily consisted of $2.4 billion of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and $1.4 billion of stock-based compensation expense.

comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA utilize an 'All Other' category to aggregate results from non-segmented items. Intel defines the composition of this category by listing specific businesses like Altera and Mobileye. NVIDIA also reports an 'All Other operating loss' line item, explaining that variances in this loss are driven by specific items like acquisition termination costs and stock-based compensation, similar to how Intel's 'All Other' captures distinct non-core financial impacts (though Intel specifies the business units while NVIDIA specifies the expense drivers).

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm operates through three reportable segments: QCT (semiconductor), QTL (licensing), and QSI (strategic investments), along with nonreportable segments like QGOV.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm explicitly disclose the existence of 'nonreportable segments' within their segment reporting structures. Intel groups results from businesses like Altera and Mobileye into its 'All Other' category which includes 'non-reportable segments'. Similarly, Qualcomm identifies specific nonreportable segments like QGOV and its cloud computing initiative alongside its reportable segments (QCT, QTL, QSI). Both companies use this classification to separate core reportable performance from smaller or strategic initiatives not given separate segment status.
